name: Blac Youngsta
notes: A front-of-beat, near-yelled, ad-lib-saturated record, and the research turns that vocal description straight into two mix parameters: **velocity kept flat and loud to match the vocal**, so `velocityTiers` compress into a narrow loud band and `humanize.velocityVar` falls to 0.05 with `quantizeStrength` at 0.97 — the tightest and flattest kit in this batch by a distance. Against that, the melodic layer is described as **high register and thin, because the mix leaves room for the ad-libs, which function as a second percussion layer** — hence the highest `melody.register` here [64,86] over a low note density, and a perc block carrying a third lane for the ad-lib function. The 808 is tuned with slides and a short-to-medium decay so the hat pattern stays audible, which is why `slideProb` is 0.30 with a 30–70 ms portamento rather than the pedal tone the classic entries use. Heavy snare rolls plus flat velocity is an unusual combination and it is why this entry has the batch's lowest `gapProb` (0.05) with a high `descendProb` — the roll is continuous and falls rather than stuttering. Harmony is one chord under a single bright motif, so `impliedByRiff` carries the chord part. ⚠ `low`: the research rates it medium-low and says **all beat parameters are modern-Memphis lane inferences** — `session.bpm` (70–82 half-time = 140–164 straight, marked [LOW-CONF]), the kick placement and the hat base are all inferred. Only the Gate 1 chart and certification facts and the vocal character are sourced. ⚠ The `i–VI` and `i–VII` families are INFERRED; the research describes one chord, and the two moving families carry a sixth of the drone's weight between them so the chord and bass parts have somewhere to go. ⚠ The bass ceiling came down from 42 to 41 so it stays under a chord part that starts at 42 — `coherence.rs` requires the highest bass note to sit at or below the lowest chord note, and this model overlapped by 1. ⚠ `anticipationProb` raised to 0.15. With `mirror_kick` against a fully locked 808 both parts take every kick, so every bass onset lands exactly on an 808 onset — `coherence.rs` calls that one line played twice rather than two parts locking. The lock is the style and is untouched; the anticipation is what makes them two parts. ⚠ **The countermelody reached only 969 distinct answers in 1000 seeds against a floor of 980**, so it was given range: densityRatio 0.45. A counter is combinatorial in the styles it may pick, its density against the melody, and the phrase length it answers inside — one style over a thin density inside a single phrase length has almost nothing a seed can vary.
